media.title: Network Topology — Segmented LAN
media.caption: Router to core switch to VLAN-segmented access switches. Watch packets flow: servers on VLAN 10 (10.0.10.0/24) and clients on VLAN 20 (10.0.20.0/24) never share a broadcast domain.
media.alt: Animated network topology with VLAN segmentation and packet flow

media.title: VLAN Trunking — 802.1Q Tag Insertion
media.caption: See an Ethernet frame cross a trunk link as the 4-byte 802.1Q tag (TPID 0x8100 + VLAN ID) is inserted. Access ports send untagged frames; trunks carry tagged frames for multiple VLANs.
media.alt: Animated 802.1Q VLAN tag insertion on a trunk link

media.title: Active Directory OU Hierarchy
media.caption: The corp.local domain tree: top-level OUs for Workstations, Servers, Users, and Service Accounts, with sub-OUs beneath. Note the GPO linked at the Workstations OU — policies flow down the tree.
media.alt: Animated Active Directory organizational unit hierarchy

media.title: VPN Tunnel Establishment — IKE Phase 1 and 2
media.caption: Watch a site-to-site tunnel come up: IKE Phase 1 negotiates the secure channel (UDP 500), Phase 2 negotiates the IPsec SAs (UDP 4500 NAT-T), then encrypted packets flow through the tunnel.
media.alt: Animated IKE Phase 1/Phase 2 VPN tunnel establishment

media.title: RAID Levels — Striping, Mirroring, Parity
media.caption: RAID 0 stripes for speed (n×d, no redundancy). RAID 1 mirrors for safety (n/2 usable). RAID 5 stripes with rotating parity ((n−1)×d, survives one disk loss). RAID 10 mirrors then stripes ((n/2)×d, fast and safe).
media.alt: Animated RAID 0/1/5/10 data striping, mirroring, and parity

media.title: Hyper-V Virtual Switch Types
media.caption: External: VMs and host share the physical NIC — traffic reaches the physical network. Internal: VMs talk to each other and the host only. Private: VMs talk only to each other, fully isolated.
media.alt: Animated Hyper-V external, internal, and private virtual switch traffic flow

media.title: DNS Resolution Flow
media.caption: Follow a query from client to recursive resolver to root to TLD to authoritative server, and back with the answer: 93.184.216.34. This is what happens every time you type a name instead of a number.
media.alt: Animated DNS recursive resolution from client to authoritative server

media.title: DHCP DORA Process
media.caption: Discover (broadcast: 'any DHCP server out there?'), Offer ('take 192.168.1.50'), Request ('I'll take it'), Ack ('it's yours for 8 days'). Four packets and the client has an address.

media.title: SQL Backup Chain
media.caption: Full backup Sunday, differentials Wednesday and Saturday, log backups hourly. To restore to Friday: restore the full, then the latest differential, then every log after it — in order.
media.alt: Animated SQL Server full-differential-log backup chain and restore sequence
Animated diagram of the TCP three-way handshake showing SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK packets with sequence numbers between client and server
media.caption: SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK with animated packets and live sequence/acknowledgment numbers. The ACK is always received-seq + 1.
media.title: TCP 3-Way Handshake — Animated

media.alt: Animated diagram of the six-message Kerberos ticket exchange between client, KDC, and file server
media.caption: AS-REQ/AS-REP → TGS-REQ/TGS-REP → AP-REQ across Client, KDC, and file server. Six messages, zero passwords on the wire.
media.title: Kerberos Ticket Exchange — Animated

media.alt: Animated OSI model diagram showing data encapsulation as headers are added descending the seven layers
media.caption: All seven layers with a payload that grows TCP, IP, and Ethernet headers as it descends: Segment → Packet → Frame → Bits.
media.title: OSI Model — Data Encapsulation — Animated

media.alt: Animated spanning-tree convergence diagram showing root bridge election and port state transitions
media.caption: Three switches exchange BPDUs, elect the root bridge by lowest Bridge ID, assign Root/Designated ports, and a redundant port cycles Blocking → Listening → Learning → Forwarding.
media.title: STP Convergence — Animated

media.alt: Animated GPO precedence diagram showing LSDOU layers applying in order with the OU policy winning
media.caption: Local → Site → Domain → OU apply in order over the same setting; each layer overwrites the last until the OU wins. Enforced beats Block Inheritance.
media.title: GPO Precedence — LSDOU — Animated

media.alt: Animated backup and restore flow diagram showing a weekly backup timeline, LSN chain, and restore sequence
media.caption: A week of FULL, differential, and log backups on an unbroken LSN chain, then the restore: FULL → DIFF → LOGs in order, NORECOVERY until the final log.
media.title: Backup → Restore Flow — Animated

media.alt: Animated side-by-side comparison of manual static IP configuration versus automated DHCP leasing
media.caption: Side-by-side race: hand-typed static IPs crawl in and collide on a duplicate address, while the DHCP server leases a whole row in seconds.
media.title: Static vs DHCP — Animated

media.alt: Animated firewall ACL diagram showing packets evaluated top-down against rules with first-match allow and deny outcomes
media.caption: Two packets walk the same rule list top-down: one is denied at the broad DENY rule, the other reaches the ALLOW — rule order is everything.
media.title: Firewall ACL — First Match Wins — Animated
